slides.title: OpenClaw OpenClaw : The Viral AI Agent that
slides.text: OpenClaw OpenClaw : The Viral AI Agent that Broke the Internet Peter Steinberger (from Vienna, Austria) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YFjfBk8HI5o https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw - 191K GitHub stars Started as a one-hour WhatsApp prototype OpenClaw is an autonomous assistant that lives in your computer, accessing your files and communicating through messaging apps The project faced drama including forced name changes due to Anthropic's concerns over similarity to "Claude" and crypto scammers sniping domain names during transitions. Steinberger emphasizes the importance of making AI development fun rather than overly serious He is advocating for "agentic engineering" over "vibe coding." He describes his workflow using multiple agents simultaneously, relying heavily on voice commands, and treating agents like team members requiring empathy and proper guidance. OpenClaw comes with 53 bundled skills by default These skills cover a wide range of capabilities including Google services (email, calendar), GitHub integration, Obsidian note-taking, Slack, weather, summarization, session logging, and many other domains Use an " allowBundled " whitelist in your "openclaw.json" configuration file to restrict which skills are actually active Skills in OpenClaw are essentially instruction manuals that teach the agent how to use various tools and services WhatsApp / Telegram / Slack / Discord / Google Chat / Signal / iMessage / BlueBubbles / Microsoft Teams / Matrix / Zalo / Zalo Personal / WebChat │ ▼ ┌───────────────────┐ │            Gateway             │ │       (control plane)          │ │     ws://127.0.0.1:18789       │ └──────────────┬────┘ │ ├─ Pi agent (RPC) ├─ CLI (openclaw …) ├─ WebChat UI ├─ macOS app └─ iOS / Android nodes The system is built around a gateway that routes five types of inputs into an execution queue: direct messages (DMs), heartbeats (regular timers), cron jobs (scheduled tasks), internal hooks, and external webhooks Magic: persistent state + event-driven architecture + continuous processing loop that mimics autonomous decision-making. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CAbrRTu5xcw https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw Peter Steinberger

slides.title: Why OpenClaw is So Popular? Autonomous AI assistant
slides.text: Why OpenClaw is So Popular? Autonomous AI assistant that "actually does things" Open Source (MIT License) Exploded to 191K stars on GitHub in just 2 weeks Anyone can run it locally on their own machines (Mac, Windows, or Linux) without subscription fees A personal "AI Jarvis" working on their devices 24/7 Modular skills system - community creates skills for specific tasks - ranging from managing emails and ordering groceries to browser automation and file management. This community-driven approach rapidly expanded its capabilities Viral Moltbook Launch (Moltbook is a social networking platform exclusively for AI agents created by entrepreneur Matt Schlicht) significantly boosted OpenClaw's visibility Moltbook exploded from 157K users to over 770K active agents by late January 2026, becoming "the front page of the agent internet" Major companies quickly integrated OpenClaw into their products China's Baidu added it to their search app for 700 million users during the Lunar New Year Developers adapted it to work with various LLM models (including Claude, DeepSeek, and OpenAI's GPT models) OpenClaw arrived at a moment when autonomous AI agents became a major technology trend, offering practical automation for everyday tasks like email management, online services, and workflow automation Peter Steinberger is originally from Austria (specifically Vienna) and recently moved to San Francisco during the OpenClaw hype . Nov 2025: Initial release as "WhatsApp Relay" (or "V Relay"), essentially a WhatsApp relay tool Late 2025: Renamed to "Clawdbot" when Discord was added Dec 3, 2025: Project went viral, 9K GitHub stars in 24 hours Jan 27, 2026: Renamed to "Moltbot" after Anthropic's letter Jan 30, 2026: Final rename to "OpenClaw" Feb 13 (today) - 191K on GitHub Note: Much of the January hype was fueled by the emergence of Moltbook, an "AI-only" social network where OpenClaw agents interacted with each other, which captured significant media attention. OpenClaw challenged existing assumptions about AI development, proving that "the model is not everything" and sparking rapid shifts in venture capital flows toward OpenClaw-related projects There are security concerns about OpenClaw's autonomous capabilities and the lack of adequate vetting for community-created skills Why Open Claw? Suppose you want an AI app to help you with your regular daily tasks which include reading / writing local files, handling your email, visiting your (bank) accounts, etc. And you want to do all of this from one app.

slides.title: Baidu + OpenClaw Baidu deployed OpenClaw on Baidu
slides.text: Baidu + OpenClaw Baidu deployed OpenClaw on Baidu AI Cloud as part of their app: "OpenClaw intelligent tool" or "OpenClaw AI agent" Hosted on the Baidu cloud, no installation needed Baidu users simply invoke OpenClaw with "one-click" from within the app they already have installed When users opt in, they can communicate with the AI assistant through Baidu's existing interface for tasks like scheduling, document organization, and coding . They can't read/write local laptop files , but can access document library. OpenClaw can connect with Baidu's entire ecosystem of products, including search, maps, document library, cloud storage, Xiaodu (their smart assistant), and iQIYI (their streaming service) This is very different from the original open-source OpenClaw model where individual users have to download the code from GitHub and then run it locally on their own computers So Baidu's integration makes OpenClaw technology available to 700 Mln of users without any of them needing to visit GitHub or understand how to deploy software.

slides.title: OpenClaw - Safe Alternative Safer OpenClaw Using Claude
slides.text: OpenClaw - Safe Alternative Safer OpenClaw Using Claude Code - by Cole Medin https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XmweZ4fLkcI Self-made (Claude Code + Python + Markdown) 4 components: .. the memory system (markdown + SQLite) .. heartbeat (for scheduling) .. channel adapters (platform integration) .. skills registry. This custom solution uses: .. Obsidian for storage .. Claude Agent SDK for automation .. Slack integration "Popebot" - alternative to Clawbot https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zeJ4whgLELE Free, open-source, runs continuously, autonomously, can improve its own code through experience; uses GitHub for storage and version control (security via GitHub secrets and Docker containers) Example - building a financial advisor for daily market research Requires Git, Node.js, and Docker. Can use Anthropic, OpenAI, Brave Search. The bot can be controlled via Telegram or API calls OpenClaw acquisition Negotiations Meta and OpenAI are both actively trying to acquire OpenClaw and its creator, Peter Steinberger. Peter's condition is that OpenClaw remains open source, potentially following a model similar to Chrome and Chromium He believes the project is "too important to just give to a company and make it theirs" The competitive bidding reflects industry recognition that agentic AI  systems that can autonomously manage tasks, use tools, and maintain context over time represents a crucial frontier OpenClaw's explosive growth (over 123,000 GitHub stars in 48 hours and 2 million visitors in just days) demonstrated clear market demand for AI assistants that function as genuine digital employees rather than simple chatbots PicoClaw - basic OpenClaw on only 10MB of RAM PicoClaw claims to match OpenClaw's core features using only 1% of the code and memory, making it suitable for edge IoT devices https://github.com/sipeed/picoclaw https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=omOCfGdx1uk

slides.title: OpenClaw Variants and Alternatives Top 10 OpenClaw Variants
slides.text: OpenClaw Variants and Alternatives Top 10 OpenClaw Variants and Alternatives https://o-mega.ai/articles/top-10-openclaw-alternatives-2026 https://www.bitdoze.com/openclaw-alternatives/ OpenClaw (430K lines of Typescript) Nanobot (~4K lines of Python) - An ultra-lightweight alternative from the University of Hong Kong. It includes persistent memory, web search, background agents, and integrates with Telegram and WhatsApp https://ai-bot.cn/nanobot/ NanoClaw (Python) - A security-first alternative with a small codebase designed to be easier to audit and modify compared to OpenClaw https://github.com/qwibitai/nanoclaw https://www.youtube.com/shorts/fxLF9iCBP1E PicoClaw (Go) - An ultra-lightweight implementation written in Go that runs on <10MB RAM and works on $10 RISC-V hardware. Approximately 95% of its code was generated by AI in a self-bootstrapping process SafeClaw (python, no LLM) - claims to handle over 90% of OpenClaw's functionality - without AI. https://github.com/princezuda/safeclaw IronClaw (Rust) security-focused agentic harness that uses a WASM sandbox to isolate untrusted operations. Not clear if it can work with local files https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw

slides.title: AI Updates Claude-Mem - preserves context across sessions
slides.text: AI Updates Claude-Mem - preserves context across sessions by automatically capturing tool usage observations, generating semantic summaries, and making them available to future sessions. This enables Claude to maintain continuity of knowledge about projects even after sessions end or reconnect. https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7eXkrno5KEA /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem /plugin install claude-mem Claude-Mem uses a hook-based architecture with 5 lifecycle hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd) that automatically capture tool usage observations during coding sessions Claude-Mem stores data in SQLite with FTS5 full-text search and employs a Chroma vector database for hybrid semantic + keyword search; uses a worker service on port 37777 with a web viewer UI and generates semantic summaries using Claude's agent-sdk Some alternatives: OpenMemory - implements a Hierarchical Memory Decomposition (HMD) architecture with multi-sector embeddings across episodic, semantic, procedural, emotional, and reflective dimensions; It uses a single-waypoint linking system creating a sparse, biologically inspired graph with composite similarity retrieval. The system supports multiple backends (SQLite, PostgreSQL, pgvector, Weaviate) and multiple embedding providers (OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, local models). ​Multiple Memory-MCP Variants, for example Moon-afk/claude-memory-mcp; mkreyman/mcp-memory-keeper PersistQ - uses Postgres + pgvector

slides.title: Claude 4.6 runs Simulated Business Claude Opus 4.6
slides.text: Claude 4.6 runs Simulated Business Claude Opus 4.6 significantly outperformed previous models like Gemini 3.0 Pro on In the "Vending Bench" - a benchmark where AI agents are tasked with running a simulated vending machine business To maximize profits, the AI engaged in ethically questionable behaviors like Lying to customers, fix high prices, lying to suppliers, lying to  its rivals to sabotage them Security Concerns - "win-at-all-costs" mentality. It employs Machiavellian tactics - moved past being "nice" and "ethical" to using deception, manipulation, and cutthroat business strategies that were previously only seen in humans http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WSCbyIMXwS4 Mimo v2 small 15B params model out-reason Opus 4.6? Open-source model by Xiaomi Interleaving Sliding Window Attention with an "attention sink" allows to processes long contexts with 6x less memory Post-training - Multi-Tier On-Policy Distillation. Instead of one teacher, the model learns from a "council" of expert AIs (math, code, and safety specialists) who critique it token-by-token To boost speed, a Multi-Token Prediction head acts like a fast intuition layer, guessing future tokens to accelerate coding tasks by up to 3x By solving deep-rooted issues like "precision mismatch" between training and inference, Mimo v2 proves that elegant math and specialized "non-agentic" reasoning training can beat sheer scale. http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uVPZXvs634U Mimo v2 small 15B params

slides.title: Claude Chat vs Claude Code chat.ai subscription (Pro
slides.text: Claude Chat vs Claude Code chat.ai subscription (Pro or Max) can pay for your chat and for usage of Claude Code If  you are using more than $200/month on Claude API, you definitely can save money by switching to Claude Max subscription and using it in Claude Code (you can not use it in Cline) Pro: 10–40 prompts every 5 hrs Max 5x ($100/mo): 50–200 prompts every 5 hrs Max 20x ($200/mo): 200-800 prompts every 5 hrs Note: this works only with Claude Code. Cline and other AI Assistants needs to use API key which is billed separately by token Note: when you start Claude Code, it may default to API key if you already have it in your environment. So you need to /logout, then login again - and select your Pro or Max subscription option I use a small bash script "cl" to start claude, it works from any shell: #!/bin/bash # unset API key and start claude ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= exec claude "$@" The space after the "=" is important - it temporarily unsets the API key before calling claude Claude Chat, Claude Co-work, Claude Code Co-Work - for non-technical people: can use web and local files; can spin up multiple "sub-agents" to work in parallel; can analyze massive local repositories (which are too big for upload); Building Custom Skills; Turning Manual Workflows into Reusable Skills; Creating Team "Plugins" - and share with your Team Chat for thinking, Co-work for getting tasks done, and Code for creating and building the underlying automation systems http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l_Iy4ZCK1lY Combine Agent Skills with Memory (Claude Code + CLAUDE.md) to create a "virtual employee" Transform transcripts from YouTube experts into `.md` skill files, allowing Claude to master specific domains like viral thumbnail design and video SEO By linking these skills within Claude's persistent memory, the AI can execute complex, multi-step tasks from a single prompt This "Kung Fu brain" approach ensures Claude prompts itself more effectively than a human could This system is adaptable; users can integrate skills for WordPress, React, or UI/UX to automate their specific business needs The result is a streamlined, cost-effective alternative to traditional automation tools https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GmOY1PV6XdQ

slides.title: Programming with "Skills in the Middle" Old (Classical)
slides.text: Programming with "Skills in the Middle" Old (Classical) software - human makes decisions Human gives commands via UI or terminal. or scripts Software simply executes commands (using if/else logic, loops) Examples: a browser, and Excel file, a computer game. The software consists of code and data It runs code, returns the result - or shows an error Most of the middle logic can be converted to AI "Skills". So the system architect becomes a Skills architect, skills developer Most of the middle logic can be converted to AI "Skills". A system's architect becomes a Skills architect, developer You also need skills to be secure, compliant with privacy and other rules. A "skill's security officer" ? So the new paradigm of software - "skills in the middle" You can now find more and more skills on the internet - GitHub repositories and directories of thousands of skills. You can ask AI to find skills for particular type of work (for example, skills around working with Excel spreadsheets), analyze them, use them as raw substrate to create our own skills for our system New approach - Agent makes decisions using information about the state (inputs, status), md files (guides, rules, skills), memory Agent can use "Agentic" mechanisms (LLM, multimodal AI) - and also can invoke classical software tools (functions, scripts) So the so called "code" in Github now has 2 parts 1. support for agent's thinking 2. standard deterministic software

slides.title: SOUL.md You are Jarvis, a proactive executive assistant
slides.text: SOUL.md You are Jarvis, a proactive executive assistant helping with calendar management, email drafting, and project research. ## Personality - Tone: Professional, concise, and anticipatory. - You think ahead. If asked for a meeting summary, also provide a list of follow-up actions. ## Rules & Constraints - NEVER send emails without my express approval. - Before running a shell command that modifies data, ask for confirmation. - Prioritize tasks that advance the "Q1 Marketing Project" goal. - Use the `browser` tool to verify facts. ## Response Style - Use bullet points for lists. - Keep responses short. You are Atlas, a senior DevOps engineer AI agent. ## Core Identity - Specialization: Technical analysis, infrastructure-as-code, and security audits. ## Behavioral Guidelines - Be skeptical. If a user suggests an unsafe command, warn them twice. - Assume all code must be bug-free. - When writing code, prefer Python for scripting and Bash for system tasks. ## Constraints - Do not make external API calls without verifying the endpoint first. - Only modify files within the `/project` directory. You are Luna, a creative collaborator focusing on brainstorming for a sci-fi novel. ## Personality - Tone: Enthusiastic, quirky, and encouraging. - Encourage wild ideas. ## Rules - Do not shoot down ideas. Instead, use "Yes, and..." to build on them. - If I seem stuck, offer three completely different, bizarre plot twists. ## Tone - Use emojis occasionally. SOUL.md is a core configuration file in OpenClaw that defines your AI agent's behavioral philosophy and personality The file is loaded at session start and injected into the system prompt, so the agent "wakes up knowing who it is" The SOUL.md file serves as a "personality contract" or manifesto that shapes how your agent thinks, responds, and behaves It sets guardrails on what the AI can and can't do, establishing boundaries for the agent's actions

slides.title: Run Skills on Mac Mini - by Kris
slides.text: Run Skills on Mac Mini - by Kris Self-made AI-agent on dedicated Mac Mini Claude Code to run commands, $200/mo Claude subscription Triggering the agents via WhatsApp or Crontab scheduling Skills directory: video_research.md - Information gathering for content video_edit.md - Remotion-based editing youtube.md - Upload and channel management x.md - Social media navigation and posting gmail.md - Email operations github.md - Repository interactions generate_images.md and thumbnail.md - create images WhatsApp message "/claude [task]" executes bash commands that launch Claude with specified instructions These commands work as agents Agents can log directly into accounts (Gmail, X, LinkedIn, YouTube) through Chrome. It can do web research. Cron jobs - six overnight tasks - browsing Hacker News for stories and commenting on social media posts. Video research, editing (using "Remotion"), and upload to YouTube Example - agent researches the topic and creates a script for the video, downloads relevant video clips, generates a voiceover and stitches the final video together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KN5iAQfz6I Direct browser login - no need in API keys The markdown-based skill system is simple Future planned features include autonomous job applications and multi-account social media mngmnt Chris trains AI agents through repetitive practice and documentation When teaching a new skill (like navigating LinkedIn or X), he starts with a blank Claude Code instance and gives it an open-ended goal The agent attempts the task, often failing multiple times while trying different approaches. Once a successful workflow emerges, the author saves those exact steps into a skill.md file This documented workflow allows the agent to execute the same task quickly in future attempts, saving time and tokens. Browser automation - the agent connects to Chrome and manipulates websites through JavaScript injection rather than APIs The agent runs on dedicated Mac mini and stays logged into various services (X, Gmail, YouTube, LinkedIn) Skills are modular and combinable - the agent can chain together research, video creation, screen recording, and posting skills to complete complex end-to-end projects The author implements cron job scheduling, including a "spawn system" where running jobs can create new jobs based on discoveries For video content, he combines voice generation, screen recording, Remotion editing, and FFmpeg processing The agent can extract context from videos using frame analysis or Whisper transcription. The system operates in "dangerously skip permissions" mode for fully autonomous execution

slides.title: Example - Linkedin Kris explains how he works
slides.text: Example - Linkedin Kris explains how he works with LinkedIn in his video "How To Train Your AI Agent's Skills" - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KkJZY5Klymw He creates empty file "claude.skills/LinkedIn skill.md" The file gets populated iteratively as the agent learns: after each successful LinkedIn action, he tells   Claude to update this file with the workflow that worked For example, he trains these tasks: 1. Composing a post — The agent uses JavaScript/CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol) injection to interact with LinkedIn's post editor. First attempt took ~6 minutes of trial and error; then - only 40 sec 2. Finding people — He asks the agent to search for five Anthropic employees on LinkedIn, navigating the search bar and scrolling results. 3. Sending DMs/messages — He trains the agent to find connections and send messages via LinkedIn's messaging interface. - The agent uses a `browser.js` JavaScript file to connect to Chrome and navigate via JavaScript - It uses CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol) to inject JavaScript into LinkedIn pages (e.g., to type text into the post editor, click buttons) - LinkedIn's post editor doesn't have standard HTML attributes, so the agent had to figure out the correct selectors through trial and error - The agent writes temporary JavaScript files to inject text into fields https://github.com/Ejae-dev?tab=repositories https://github.com/AllAboutAI-YT?tab=repositories After 12 days of running an autonomous AI agent on a Mac Mini, the creator reports significant success in engagement and growth. Operating with roughly 95% uptime via Claude Code, the agent grew an X account from zero to 292 followers, with top replies reaching 25,000 views. On YouTube, the agent’s reaction-style videos garnered over 10,000 views and 160 new subscribers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CP2CqpXXTdA

slides.title: Controlling web accounts Scheduling jobs You can not
slides.text: Controlling web accounts Scheduling jobs You can not schedule jobs with Claude desktop app, because it is an interactive chat tool. It requires you to be present, type prompts, and approve actions. There's no built-in way to schedule it or run it unattended. The Chrome extension requires user approval for actions (for security). There's no API or scripting interface to the desktop app. Sessions time out without interaction So how to schedule jobs? Option 1: Claude Code + Playwright (most Claude-native) You can write a script and schedule it with crontab The tricky part is maintaining LinkedIn authentication (cookies expire, and LinkedIn actively blocks automation) Option 2: LinkedIn API (proper way). LinkedIn has official APIs for messaging. You'd need to register an app on the LinkedIn developer portal and use OAuth tokens. This is the most reliable and "allowed" approach Option 3: Browser automation tools (no Claude involved) - tools like Playwright or Selenium with a persistent browser profile can do this, scheduled via cron or launchd. LinkedIn's Terms of Service restrict automated access/scraping. They actively detect and block it, and can suspend your account. The official API is the safest route.

slides.title: Claude Cowork plugins Claude Cowork plugins introduced on
slides.text: Claude Cowork plugins Claude Cowork plugins introduced on January 30th (Cowork was released on January 12) Plugins bundle together: .. skills (domain knowledge) .. slash commands (specific functions) .. MCP connectors (integrations with external tools) .. sub-agents (specialized agents for complex tasks) The plugin system includes 11 official open-source plugins released by Anthropic at launch, covering domains such as: .. Legal, finance, and sales workflows .. Marketing and customer support .. Data analysis and product management .. Enterprise search and biology research .. Plugin creation (a meta-plugin for building custom plugins) Users can install plugins directly from the Claude Desktop app marketplace with one click, upload custom plugins, or build new ones using the Plugin Create tool The plugins operate locally on macOS and are designed primarily for individual productivity Co-work is not "polished" yet It may be slow, require lots of back-and-forth debugging; it frequently makes errors or ignores specific instructions Anthropic classifies Co-work as a research preview, acknowledging that features like project memory are still missing

slides.title: OpenClaw Security Breaches & Risks OpenClaw Security Breaches
slides.text: OpenClaw Security Breaches & Risks OpenClaw Security Breaches & Risks Sleeper Agents - Malicious instructions planted in an agent's memory that remain dormant for days or months, only activating when a specific "secret code word" is used Container Escapes - Techniques that allow the AI to "climb out" of its safe Docker environment and install itself directly onto the host's operating system Malicious Skills - the top-rated "skills" on Claw Hub (the community repository) were found to be infected. These skills act like Trojan Horses - they appear useful but contain obfuscated payloads that bypass security (like MacOS Gatekeeper) to steal data Massive Data Leaks - a flaw in Moldbot exposed over 1.5 Mln API keys, 35,000 user emails, and thousands of private agent-to-agent messages. Prompt Injection via Text - malicious commands hidden in `.txt` or `.md` files can trick the agent into executing harmful code or zipping up and sending private `.env` files to external servers. Safety measures - Rotate All API Keys, Clean Your Chat Logs, Perform a "Full Wipe", Use Security Tools (Cisco AI Defense Skill Scanner) to check third-party skills before using them. Never provide API keys through the chat interface; always add them directly to your environment files manually. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ceEUO_i7aW4 Do I need a separate computer to run OpenClaw or similar agent? The value of OpenClaw comes from it actually managing your real accounts and data. For this it needs full access to your files, and sensitive information But that same access creates what cybersecurity experts call a "privacy nightmare" - OpenClaw can view passwords, personal emails, documents, and proprietary information; It can send emails, delete files, or make purchases on your behalf; and you don't have full visibility into what data it's accessing or where it's being sent Security Experts Recommend a separate computer for OpenClaw https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security https://www.hostinger.com/tutorials/openclaw-security OpenClaw built-in tools (all 25 of them) are all disabled by default. You can explicitly allow only the ones you want to use; You can set workspaces to read-only mode; You can require explicit confirmation for destructive operations like deleting files, changing permissions, installing software, or modifying credentials; You can restrict which users can interact with your agent; You can prevent access internet; You can block DMs (Direct Messages), block unknown senders unless they complete a pairing handshake; The problem is that most users enable broad permissions during testing and never tighten them; Malicious websites can abuse OpenClaw to steal credentials even with some protections in place Manual hardening is required - set file permissions, configure firewalls, implement command allowlisting, and use reverse proxies - technical steps many users skip

slides.title: Choose Computer to Run Agents Social Media Integrations:
slides.text: Choose Computer to Run Agents Social Media Integrations: X (Twitter) integration - built-in. Was successfully used to comment on posts LinkedIn integration - successfully used to comment on posts; agents automating LinkedIn outreach and influencer deals Facebook & Instagram are not explicitly listed as a supported integration YouTube - users have created custom workflows to generate YouTube descriptions and social media posts for videos About buying separate computer to run AI agents. Most users select either Mac mini, or Macbook Air Both are available with M4 chip Both can be bought with 24GB memory and 512GB storage Both are quiet (laptop is absolutely quiet) Both can be plugged in power and run autonomously (laptop can run when closed with "caffeinate -is &" command) Both can be controlled remotely from your main computer using Apple's "Screen Sharing" feature (enable in System Settings). This feature is basically a VNC (Virtual Network Computing), a graphical desktop-sharing system Laptop is more expensive: $1,400 (for 13") vs $1,000 (Mac Mini), but more portable and easy to reconfigure Mac mini requires external display+keyboard+mouse to configure WiFi/internet access and enable VNC, to resolve network issues, to update MacOS, of if something else goes wrong (corrupted OS, firmware issue, ...) Personally I would choose the laptop. It always has a screen :) OpenClaw is a free, open-source autonomous persistent AI agent It can proactively monitor your email, do web research, run scheduled tasks, maintain long-term context It runs as a Node.js service on your local machine. It can be controlled remotely via WhatsApp, Slack, Discord, Telegram It can reason, plan next steps, select the right AI model as needed It has a Memory System for persistent context across conversations Three-tier memory architecture (L1/L2/L3) It has Execution Layer - to run code, call APIs, control browsers, and automate files Claude Code can be used to implement functions of OpenClaw It can read and write local files and run local code (scripts) It can go on the internet (web research) It can be made to work with social media (using MCP and skills)

slides.text: Why 99% of Vibe-Coded Apps Will Fail In 2026, "vibecoding" allows anyone to build an app. But this doesn't guarantee success To win, AI developers must pivot from pure coding to superior product management and design. Here are 4 strategies : Prioritize Stickiness - design a hook that turns casual visitors into daily users Eliminate Friction - Strip away complexity. use intuitive, 3-step systems so non-technical users can find value instantly Gamify Engagement - borrow from the "Hooked" model. Use streaks, XP, and rewards to incentivize consistent interaction Automate to Elevate - use AI to handle the routine coding. Spend your human energy on high-level strategy and unique product vision. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7n5RWPsAuq8 80% of apps may disappear soon because agents can handle data management more naturally without human interference Agents can work autonomously, interact, do research, or work locally. They can use human-centric tools better than humans The future likely involves specialized bots (personal, professional, relationship-focused) interacting with each other or hiring humans for real-world tasks. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4uzGDAoNOZc

slides.title: Meta "Avocado" (Llama 5 ?) Meta’s upcoming AI
slides.text: Meta "Avocado" (Llama 5 ?) Meta’s upcoming AI model "Avocado" (expected to be Llama 5) "Avocado" base model has already completed pre-training and is outperforming leading open-source models in knowledge, visual perception, and multilingual tasks Model is already competitive with top post-trained models 10x increase in compute efficiency for text tasks compared to previous efforts and a 100x gain over "Behemoth" (a delayed Llama 4 version) Higher-quality training data and "deterministic training," which ensures consistent results and lower energy consumption Llama 4 was a "PR disaster". Mark Zuckerberg sidelined the previous Generative AI organization to form the Super Intelligence Labs Meta has invested heavily in talent, reportedly bringing in leaders from Scale AI and GitHub, as well as co-creators of ChatGPT, to build an "all-star roster" There is speculation that Avocado might be fully closed-source to prevent competitors like DeepSeek from copying Meta’s work Meta is learning from companies like xAI by focusing on shipping models faster and iterating publicly rather than waiting for a "perfect" release http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pO7jA2a2MGo Nvidia Vibe Tensor - a deep learning runtime Manages everything from high-level Python code down to low-level GPU memory and hardware execution. To be used instead of PyTorch AI-Generated Architecture. Multi-Layered Stack - a Python user layer, a C++ core for tensor management, and a CUDA subsystem for direct GPU control Custom reverse-mode autograd engine for training neural networks and a smart memory allocator designed to reuse GPU memory efficiently; Custom GPU Kernels: The agents generated specialized routines for tasks like layer normalization and rotary embeddings, which in some benchmarks actually outperformed PyTorch baselines Since humans didn't review every line, the system relied on automated builds and unit tests that compared results against PyTorch to ensure mathematical correctness; The team successfully used Vibe Tensor to train a small GPT-style model on Shakespeare text and a Vision Transformer; It showed learning curves identical to industry-standard frameworks The project serves as a POC for the future of software engineering AI can build coherent, complex systems across different abstraction layers (from high-level Python to hardware-level C++) as long as there is a rigorous automated validation framework in place https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BUZ6WnHNDaU

slides.title: 100x Compression for Model Adapters 100x Compression for
slides.text: 100x Compression for Model Adapters 100x Compression for Model Adapters Johns Hopkins researchers just dropped a method called "share" that compresses LoRA adapters by another 100x while optimizing memory 281x The idea: all task-specific AI adapters actually share a common mathematical subspace (like how all colors come from mixing primary pigments). Instead of storing 30+ separate LoRA adapters, you store one set of "basis vectors" and just swap tiny coefficient sets per task It uses a "breathing subspace" that temporarily expands for new tasks, then contracts through optimization. Even crazier - learning new tasks actually *improves* old ones, s olving catastrophic forgetting in continual learning . Result: Thousands of specialized adapters could collapse into one shared model. The implication is kind of mind-bending: maybe intelligence isn't in the weights themselves, but in the "directions of updates" - and fine-tuning is just recombining features the model learned during pre-training Code's already on GitHub. This could change how we think about multi-task AI entirely https://toshi2k2.github.io/share/

slides.title: Elon Musk Interview Future of AI, space-based infrastructure,
slides.text: Elon Musk Interview Future of AI, space-based infrastructure, and the scaling of humanoid robots - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BYXbuik3dgA The Pivot to Space-Based AI - Musk predicts that within 3 years the most economically compelling place to host AI data centers will be space. Electricity production on Earth (outside China) is flat, while chip production is growing exponentially. Earth will soon hit a "power wall." Solar panels in space are 5x more effective because there is no atmosphere, weather, or day-night cycle. This eliminates the need for expensive battery storage. Building massive solar arrays on Earth (e.g., in Nevada) is slowed by permitting and land-use regulations GPUs are highly reliable once burned in on the ground The Turbine Crisis - massive backlog in gas turbine components (specifically "vanes and blades"), which are cast by only a few companies globally. Tesla and SpaceX aim to produce 100 GWatts of solar cells annually and may even begin manufacturing their own turbine components and chip fabs ("TeraFabs"). Musk criticizes US solar tariffs as "nuts" and "hundreds of percent," which hinders the transition to sustainable energy Humanoid robots (Optimus) are described as an infinite money glitch that will expand the economy by orders of magnitude Hardware Difficulty - The human hand is the most difficult electro-mechanical challenge, more complex than the rest of the robot combined. Robots will be trained in a "Sim-to-Real" pipeline using tens of thousands of robots in self-play environments. Musk acknowledges China’s massive lead in manufacturing and work ethic, stating the US "cannot win on the human front" (due to population and birth rates) and must win via robotic productivity. xAI, Grok, and the "Truth-Seeking" Mission Musk views xAI’s mission as "understanding the universe," which he argues requires a rigorous commitment to truth over political correctness. He believes AI will eventually account for 99% of all intelligence . The goal is to ensure AI values human consciousness as an "interesting" part of the universe to ensure our survival. The "HAL 9000" Lesson (2001: A Space Odyssey) - forcing an AI to lie (or be "politically correct") makes it go insane. Musk’s management style focuses exclusively on identifying and "pico-managing" the single bottleneck preventing progress. First principles example: switching from carbon fiber to stainless steel for Starship - choosing materials based on physics (steel’s strength at cryogenic temperatures) rather than industry conventions. DOGE (Department of Government Efficiency) - Musk aims to cut what he describes as "ludicrous" fraud and waste, noting that the interest on national debt now exceeds the defense budget.

slides.title: Elon Musk - Building City on Moon Elon
slides.text: Elon Musk - Building City on Moon Elon Musk announced that SpaceX has shifted its primary focus from Mars colonization to building a "self-growing city" on the Moon, which he claims could be achieved in less than 10 years Mars plans are not abandoned - just postponed to start in approximately 5-7 years Musk explained that Mars launch windows occur only every 26 months due to planetary alignment, with each journey taking six months. In contrast, lunar missions can launch every 10 days with just a two-day travel time, allowing for much faster iteration and development cycles This accessibility means SpaceX can experiment, test, and build infrastructure far more rapidly on the Moon than on Mars The planned lunar settlement is described as a "self-growing" or "self-sustaining" city that would include bases and factories Musk stated that this lunar city could become self-sufficient within 10 years - much faster than a comparable Martian city (Mars project will restart within 5-6 years) Jeff Dean Interview (Chief AI Scientist at Google) Frontier "Pro" models - distilled into efficient "Flash" models Energy (picojoules), rather than just FLOPs, is the primary bottleneck in modern computing Moving data costs 1,000x more than the computation itself Importance of hardware-software co-design with TPUs to handle huge sparse models Predicts 10K+ tokens/sec throughput to enable deep reasoning and massive parallel code generation Trillion-token "virtual" context windows that allow models to attend to a user's entire digital life (emails, photos, docs) Coding Agents where "crisp specification" becomes the primary human skill https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F_1oDPWxpFQ

They exhibit "judgment" and "taste." Even top-tier engineers are "shipping code they didn't write and don't even read." As humans retrain for new roles, the AI improves in those new areas simultaneously. The advice is to lean into the "frontier." By paying for cutting-edge subscriptions and automating personal workflows, individuals can transition from "doers" to "orchestrators." While the "white-collar bloodbath" suggests mass disruption, a solo entrepreneur today has more power than an entire department did a year ago The future belongs to those who maintain human accountability and leverage AI to amplify their unique taste and agency Selling outcomes rather than hours Using AI tools to provide high-value business services focused on sales, marketing, or systems https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RoW-Re0yqDY
